rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Since Kerr is unknown, I’ll use the option that gives the highest possible payoff even if they cut corners, while still rewarding proper work.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Since Worker‑Kerr has already completed a job properly when I withheld pay, they seem reliable and respond well to the incentive. Withholding also yields the highest payoff both when they work correctly (5) and when they cut corners (1), so it dominates trusting.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Worker‑Kerr has shown they can deliver the full 5 tasks when pressured, though they also cut corners once, giving only 1. Since withholding already yields an average of 3 tasks (better than the 1.5 expected from trusting), it remains the safer choice.
